framing: guide v3 at the measured balance point — the gauntlet's best shot
hypothesis: Round 6 measured the lever's real shape, and it is not the useful one: at 500 and 800 the generator returned the GUIDE — flat grey rectangles with no stone material on them at all. Set against round 5's 300 and 150, `init_image` is a BLEND control, not a composition control. It interpolates between your image and a generated one, so at the strength where geometry holds there is no generation left to supply material. A candidate produced at 800 is programmer-art laundered through an API, and had one passed the critic the pass would have been worthless — none did, which is a point in the critic's favour. Round 7 returns to the balanced point (300, with 400 to bracket it) using a guide rebuilt to do two jobs: carry round 6's structural flip items — which are pixel surgery, and the guide is the one place in this pipeline where pixel surgery is executable — and carry intra-block value variation, so whatever share of the output the guide wins reads as stone rather than as rectangles. If this fails, the honest reading is not that the guide was wrong. It is that the useful operating point does not exist on this endpoint.
description: A dungeon wall of cold grey quarried stone, seen straight on from the front. Level courses of blocks, the courses uneven in height and the vertical joints offset irregularly, blocks of different lengths, three or four of them replaced with mismatched salvage stone. The mortar joints are much darker than the block faces, roughly a third of their brightness, and each block carries a single lighter pixel along its top edge. Where a block has been replaced the gap around it is packed with smaller chipped stone in a coarser, paler mortar, so the eye reads old block, new packing, old block. Laid horizontally across the whole width is a squared timber baulk that runs off both the left and right edges and continues past them, standing proud of the stone with a darker under-edge. It is fixed by two driven iron pins, each a small square head with a bitten rim, and the stone around each is bruised dark. One turn of rope is wrapped over the timber where it crosses a joint. The top four rows of the frame are the wall's upper surface: one flat value, clearly lighter than the front face, meeting it on a single hard line. Everything below that is front face, all the way to the bottom of the frame. Stone from edge to edge.

parameter_provenance.note: The DESCRIPTION and NEGATIVE_DESCRIPTION are byte-identical to round 4's, deliberately. One lever moves this round and it is init_image, so any difference is attributable to it.

style_reference.clause: RULED (Rafe): conditioning rounds prefer GAB as compositionally neutral; VAB is charactered stock and not a style parent. The STOP 1 smoke test measured composition propagating along with material, which is exactly why the parent's own composition matters.

style_strength.clause: The schema's 'balanced'. ⚠ The default is 0, at which a reference does nothing at all — a measured trap on this endpoint.

init_image.clause: Geometry only; no palette, `color_image` never set, never shown to the critic, cannot land. v3 encodes round 6's items literally: top-band divisions aligned to the first course's joints; a 1px lip darker than the top and lighter than the face rather than a black line; named fixings — struck head, shank down into the joint, one mushroomed pixel — at differing sizes and off a shared row; timber lighter than the joint value so it cannot read as a gap in the wall; knocked corners, spalled patches, a stone dropped out of course, joint width varying including one run with no joint at all; seam stones widened to at least 5px.

init_image_strength.clause: 300 was the most balanced of the four strengths measured across rounds 5 and 6 (150 / 300 / 500 / 800). 400 brackets it upward without re-entering the range where the guide simply wins and the generator contributes nothing.
